name: Russian Push-Up
summary: An advanced calisthenics push-up variation where you transition from the bottom of a push-up onto your forearms and rock forward back onto your hands before pressing up.

setup: Assume a high plank position with your hands roughly shoulder-width apart and your body in a rigid, straight line from head to heels.
Engage your abdominals, squeeze your glutes, and tuck your pelvis into a neutral alignment.
steps: Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, stopping an inch above the ground as in the bottom of a standard push-up.
Shift your weight backward, dropping your forearms and elbows flat onto the ground while maintaining a rigid plank.
Drive your palms aggressively into the floor and shift your body weight forward, popping off your forearms back onto your hands at the bottom of the push-up position.
Press forcefully through your hands to extend your elbows and return to the high plank lockout.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower down and shift onto your forearms; exhale forcefully as you drive back up onto your hands and press out to the starting position.
cues: Drive the ground away with your palms

common_faults.fault: Sagging the hips during the transition onto and off the forearms.
common_faults.correction: Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes tightly to keep the torso completely rigid throughout the shift.

common_faults.fault: Flaring the elbows out to the sides.
common_faults.correction: Keep the elbows tucked close to the ribs to safely load the triceps and shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Pushoff hesitation leading to an asymmetrical heave off the floor.
common_faults.correction: Build momentum with an explosive palm-drive and practice the movement from the knees first if necessary.

precautions: Place a cushioned exercise mat under your forearms to protect your elbows during the drop.
